column6: Robert Prestley,,,2026-09-24,"Hurricane Threats and Impacts (HTI) graphics communicate the spatial extent and severity of tropical cyclone hazards but provide limited information about when hazards will arrive, creating challenges for time-sensitive protective decision-making. We evaluated whether adding arrival time information to redesigned HTI-like graphics improves temporal comprehension, influences risk perception and protective actions, and is perceived as usable. column7: Cheng-Hsuan Lu,,,2026-09-09,"Accurate evaluation of both observations and forecasts is essential for advancing atmospheric composition research and improving operational prediction. Traditionally, this has relied on separate workflows with product-specific preprocessing, often limiting reproducibility and creating inconsistencies between models and observational datasets or across different products. Modern data assimilation systems provide precise observation operators for mapping model variables into observation space, yet these capabilities remain underutilized outside assimilation. Here, we demonstrate how the Joint Effort for Data assimilation Integration (JEDI) framework addresses this gap by offering a unified, modular, and model-agnostic system that integrates data assimilation with systematic evaluation.
